project.label: SecretAgent — embeddable agent runtime and its desktop agent
project.purpose: Extract the best part of four agent harnesses (DeepSeek Harness, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Onyx) into a portable C library for an embeddable agent, and the desktop agent that runs it.

atlas-root.label: Embeddable agent runtime and its desktop agent
atlas-root.description: A synthesis of the best parts of four symlink'd agent harnesses, rebuilt as a portable C library (embeddable in any host language/environment) plus the desktop agent that runs it, with WaveDB as the durable floor. What each donor contributes (design rationale in docs/chat.json): DeepSeek Harness (./deepseek-harness) — the spine: log-is-source-of-truth, the loop, the guarded tool pipeline; Prime Agent (./prime-agent) — the shape: scoped frames, encapsulation, memory hierarchy, /refine; Claude Code (./claude-code-source-code) — the escalation pattern (plan → ask → act); Onyx (./onyx) — the persona: its response instructions distilled into the loadable persona text (the 'hammer' spec, chat.json message 4148) — and WaveDB (pre-existing, done) as the substrate. All work must stay cross-platform (Linux and Windows green) and embeddable; portability is an invariant of every record, not a separate slice. Layer traceability: L0 WaveDB substrate (done), L1 unified log/tree, L2 frame/scope + surface API, L3 the loop, L4 tool pipeline + interpreter-as-a-tool, L5 persona + escalation as loadable text. The extracted liboffs actor runtime (actor, mailbox, scheduler, refcounter, platform shims) and its 58 passing tests are the existing foundation.
atlas-root.completionRoute: Four delivered slices with independent review per record: the runtime executes agent code without blocking, sessions survive restarts replayably, sessions subdivide into an accountable agent tree, and the desktop agent drives real work on top of the library. Cross-platform builds and the full gtest suite stay green at every completion.

execute-agent-code-without-blocking.label: Execute agent code without blocking the runtime
execute-agent-code-without-blocking.description:
An actor frame can execute Python in a live CPython subinterpreter while the actor keeps processing messages: EXECUTE is enqueued to the interpreter thread, log/status messages stream out to the parent live, and a RESULT returns corr-matched when the cell finishes. The interpreter is a bound tool, never the substrate; a swappable backend keeps C extensions that cannot live in a subinterpreter usable via a subprocess path. This is L4's execution verb on the L3 runtime spine. If cut, the runtime routes and persists but never computes — agents cannot close the loop on their own output. MILESTONE (pyrt layer delivered): non-blocking subinterpreter EXECUTE with live
 log/status streaming, corr-matched RESULT, lazy boot, pool cap, idle eviction,
 cooperative interrupt (forced paths inert per pinned 3.12.13 verification),
 subprocess fallback with fd discipline. Remaining for slice completion:
 Windows build (PCBuild ExternalProject branch), streaming-per-cell attribution (LOG/STATus payloads carry no corr today), review records per lifecycle.

completionEvidence: A running actor answers interrupt/control messages while a slow Python cell executes on its subinterpreter thread (cooperative: honored at cell boundaries only; a running cell is not preemptible on the pinned 3.12 chain)
Python code posts log/status messages whose bytes are attributed per cell and appear live before completion
A RESULT message returns with a correlation id matching the EXECUTE request
Execution backend is swappable (subinterpreter primary, subprocess fallback)
Cross-platform: Linux and Windows builds of the full gtest suite pass

remember-session-across-restarts.label: Survive restarts with a replayable session log
remember-session-across-restarts.description: Sessions live as WaveDB subtrees: events at sessions/<sid>/events/<seq>, lineage at meta/parent, depth at meta/depth. Every state mutation is both a store write and a logged event (one atomic batch), so the log is the single source of truth and views (message history, tree) are projections. RECUT (2026-09-29): the frame-tree slice builds state directly on WaveDB (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md), so this slice is now the kill-and-replay VERIFICATION, not a build: rebuild with a fresh boot, reverse-scan seq restore, replay-derived context, recovery from non-compacted WAL. Sessions live as WaveDB subtrees: events at sessions/<sid>/events/<seq>, lineage at meta/parent, depth at meta/depth. Verified WaveDB facts that shape the verification (docs/wavedb-exploration.md): batch atomicity spans subtrees as one WAL_BATCH/txn (capped by wal_config.max_file_size, 128 KB default); scan resume is seek-based half-open; durability at ack is a wal_sync_mode choice; seq keys zero-padded; lineage = graph SPO/POS per-hop scans; one WaveDB per process (frames = subtrees of the single root database); no clone/snapshot needed (fork = lineage pointer + new subtree). KILL-AND-RESUME EVIDENCE (2026-09-30): the proof test exists and runs — TestLoop.TestRestartReplayRestoresSeqAndContext (test/test_loop.cpp) writes a session to a scratch-disk WaveDB (msg.append + ctx remember), closes the store, reopens it, and resumes the SAME sid with frame_resume: birth record is required loudly before any write, recall resolves the remembered value across the restart, the replayed msg.append and ctx snapshot reach the next turn's derived context through the injected model vtable, and a post-resume append lands at a seq strictly past every pre-restart event (asserted through a third session's view due to the open documented WaveDB defect below). Open finding from the verification, on the record: in WaveDB CONCURRENT mode a write committed after a reopen is durable (a fresh session sees and replays it) but INVISIBLE to the same session's own scans and point-gets — the test documents and works around it with a third-session assertion. Suite state: 116 ctest green (ON and ASan under setarch -R), 76 on the OFF build, valgrind clean on the frame/loop/pyrt binaries. If cut, agent runs die with the process — no audit trail, no continuity, and log-as-safety never holds.

completionEvidence: A session persists to WaveDB and reconstructs fully (events, lineage, tree projection) after a mid-run process restart
A state mutation and its event land in one atomic transaction (no window where state moved but the log did not)
Kill-and-resume test drives the same session forward post-restart under the full ctest suite
Cross-platform: Linux and Windows builds and test runs pass

subdivide-session-into-accountable-agent.label: Subdivide sessions into an accountable agent tree
subdivide-session-into-accountable-agent.description: RECUT (2026-09-29): the frame-tree slice (drive-model-driven-frame-tree) built spawn/report/admission semantics; this slice is now the ACCOUNTABILITY VERIFICATION at tree scale (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md): parent context grows by exactly one report event per child regardless of child work volume; the frame tree derives reconstructably from lineage pointers; no #819-style scoping blind spot (children see inherited ctx only via the resolve walk, never local); compaction stays per-frame. If cut, tree sessions lose accountability guarantees at any real depth/fan-out.

completionEvidence: A spawned subagent runs in its own subtree and its report (not its transcript) lands in the parent's log
A parent's context grows by exactly one report per child, independent of child work volume
The frame tree derives reconstructably from lineage pointers in the event log
State not exposed by the parent's surface API is unaddressable from the child (the #819 scoping blind spot demonstrably absent)
Cross-platform: Linux and Windows builds and test runs pass

run-agent-as-desktop.label: Run the agent from the desktop
run-agent-as-desktop.description: A desktop/CLI client embeds the C library and drives real agent sessions end to end: frames run, code executes, sessions persist and subdivide, and results come back. Persona and escalation load as text modules (plan → ask → act) shaping the loop — the assistant's behavior is text, versionable and checkable, not compiled in. Provenance: the persona text is distilled from the Onyx harness's response instructions (./onyx; the 'hammer' persona spec in docs/chat.json message 4148), and the escalation gate design is lifted from the Claude Code source (./claude-code-source-code). This is L3+L5 and the moment the runtime becomes a product anyone can drive. If cut, the library exists but nothing runs it: there is no desktop agent.

completionEvidence: A desktop/CLI client built on the library spawns a frame, executes code, persists the session, and returns a report in one live session
Persona and escalation load as text modules and demonstrably change a real session's behavior (plan → ask → act gate observable in the log)
A second, non-C host (or the interpreter tool path) can embed the same library through the ABI and drive a session — evidence of portability, not a second implementation
Cross-platform: one client codebase builds and runs on Linux and Windows

drive-model-driven-frame-tree.label: Drive a model-driven frame tree on WaveDB
drive-model-driven-frame-tree.description: The turn loop, one OpenAI-compatible model client (single execute tool, PA-verified single-tool RLM shape), the four bridge verbs as actor behaviors (remember/recall/spawn/report) — in-process, no wire protocol — admission-only spawn/report, frame state as WaveDB subtrees of one root database per process, one atomic root batch per effect (event + state + lineage triples). Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-frame-tree-model-loop-design.md. Absorbs the build that S003/S004 would have front-loaded; S004's accountability invariants and S003's replay proof verify this work rather than building it. MILESTONE (2026-09-30, turn loop + model client + demo): the model-driven round trip runs end to end — frame store on WaveDB subtrees, turn loop (src/Frame/loop.c: derive-from-events per turn, model call, tool path to a real pyrt cell, content path, loud control events), OpenAI-compatible client (src/Frame/model.c, single execute tool, both tool_call argument shapes), HTTP client with chunked decode (src/Net/http.c), four bridge verbs. Evidence: demo CLI (tools/frame-demo, one top frame on a real scratch-disk WaveDB against local Ollama) — commit 5d7aedf + smoke; scripted-loop tests without network — TestLoop suite injects the model vtable (cell-run-and-report, steering reorder between turns, loud turn-limit cap); restart/replay proof — TestLoop.TestRestartReplayRestoresSeqAndContext (scratch-disk db, close, reopen, frame_resume: recall across the restart, replayed msg.append + ctx reach the next derive, seq continues strictly past pre-restart events); opt-in live integration gate — TestLiveLoop.TestLiveOllamaRememberAndReportWave (registered unconditionally, GTEST_SKIP unless SA_TEST_OLLAMA_URL is set). Suite: 116 ctest green (ON and ASan under setarch -R), 76 on the wavedb/python-free OFF build; valgrind clean on the frame/loop/pyrt binaries via symbol-keeping --strip-debug copies. Open constraint found by the live gate: model.c's fixed 30 s completion timeout (compile-time constant, no override seam) loses every tool-calling turn against the local gemma4 (60-90 s per turn, correct code otherwise) — the gate against the upstream-degraded cloud tags shows the same transport-failure shape; raising that seam is a model-client change, not a loop/test one.

completionEvidence: A model-driven session runs end to end from the demo CLI against a configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint (local Ollama), with every effect an atomic root batch (event + state + lineage)
The four bridge verbs round-trip corr-matched: remember/recall/spawn/report as actor behaviors
Spawn is admission-only with fail-loud depth validation; children report exactly one event up
Unit tests drive the full loop with the injected model vtable (no network)
Cross-platform: Linux green; Windows tracked on slice 1's record
